rs-tf-doe.front: Common tracking mistake about which trail to follow?
rs-tf-doe.back: Following the first tracks you see, often a doe and fawns wandering.

rs-tf-eyes.front: Where do your eyes go while tracking?
rs-tf-eyes.back: Glance down at the next print, then look 40 to 100 m ahead.

rs-tf-3-10.back: 3 seconds on the track, 10 seconds on the cover ahead (Tip).

rs-tf-light.front: How do you see faint tracks?
rs-tf-light.back: Get low and look toward a low side light. Shadows show the print.
rs-tf-light.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Light and tracks. With light from behind you the track looks flat and is hard to see. With low light from the side, shadows fill the print and it stands out. Get low and look toward the light.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Use the light</text>

</svg>

rs-tf-noon.front: Why is midday hard for tracking?
rs-tf-noon.back: Overhead sun flattens tracks; no shadows.

rs-tf-stick.back: A stick or ski pole with 2 bands set at step and stride. Sweep it from the last track to find the next.
rs-tf-stick.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Track stick step 2: put the stick tip on the last clear track and lay it along the line of travel. The next track of the same foot should be near the stride band.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="300" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">2. Lay it on the line</text>

</svg>

rs-tf-stick-reset.front: Why reset the track stick bands?
rs-tf-stick-reset.back: Stride changes with terrain and fatigue.

rs-tf-lost.back: Back to the last clear print, flag it, circle about 10 m, then 20 m.

rs-tf-wander.front: Why not walk on ahead when you lose a trail?
rs-tf-wander.back: You stamp out the next print and add a second set of tracks.

rs-tf-crunch.back: Walk like a deer: a few quick steps, then stop (Hal Blood).

rs-tf-downwind.back: Leave it and loop around so your scent does not reach the deer.

rs-tf-hook.back: It may be bedding or watching its back trail. Stop, glass, swing wide.

rs-tf-range.front: Why can a 2 day old buck track still pay off?
rs-tf-range.back: White tailed bucks often stay in about 26 to 31 km² (Benoit lore).

rs-tf-found.back: Pin the truck, record a GPS track, set a turnaround time, tell someone.

rs-tf-flaw.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 292" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Memory hooks. Glance down, look ahead: the deer is ahead, not at your feet. Lost it? Flag, circle, widen: 10 metres, then 20. Its pace sets your pace: feeding means slow right down.">
